page: Microsoft Azure HB176-96rs_v4 is an x86_64 high-performance computing instance operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The virtual machine provides 96 dedicated vCPUs backed by 768 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 8 GB per core. The server includes 4,355 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, support for Premium Storage, and RDMA networking capabilities to facilitate high-bandwidth, low-latency inter-node communication.

The hardware configuration provides dedicated compute resources without onboard GPU acceleration. With 8 GB of RAM per core, the instance balances high core density against large memory arrays, ensuring that multi-threaded processes remain supplied with substantial per-core data allocations. The integrated local NVMe SSD volume offers high-capacity temporary workspace directly attached to the host, removing storage throughput bottlenecks during high-frequency read and write cycles.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the inclusion of 4,355 GB of NVMe storage and built-in RDMA support avoids the need to provision auxiliary high-speed scratch disks or separate clustering add-ons. The server is well positioned for scale-out high-performance computing tasks, large fluid dynamics calculations, molecular modeling, complex finite element analysis, and memory-heavy distributed batch processing.
